plan.title: 20-gene signature score vs time-to-event, adjusted for case/control
plan.analytical_narrative: The question is whether a per-sample score of the study's 20-gene signature (signature/signature_genes.csv, 20 symbols, no weights, no direction) associates with time to event in this 120-sample human tumour-biopsy cohort (60 cases vs 60 controls), after accounting for case/control status. The inputs are a 12000 x 121 gene-level count matrix from Salmon whose length-correction state the record does not state, and a 120 x 4 sample table carrying condition, time and event. The plan is therefore a short, linear chain rather than a discovery workflow: (T1S1) sample-structure QC on the blind VST — PCA on the 500 most variable genes, sample-distance heatmap, library sizes — coloured by condition and by event, so any outlier or structure that would drive a spurious survival signal is visible before any model; (T1S2) filterByExpr on the counts with condition as the group, then TMM scaling factors and logCPM, which is the appropriate normalization for a cohort of this size and the log-scale input a rank-based scorer expects; (T3S1) UCell rank-based scoring of the 20-gene signature per sample on the logCPM matrix, with the number of the 20 genes actually present in the filtered matrix reported explicitly — a signature missing genes is a different signature — and a singscore score computed alongside as a sensitivity check because a rank-based score of one sample should not depend on the other samples; (T3S5) the inferential step, a Cox proportional-hazards model of time/event on the standardized signature score with condition in the same model, the score kept continuous (no median or optimized cut before the test), scaled Schoenfeld residuals for the PH check, event/censoring counts and median follow-up stated before the model, plus a score x condition interaction test to separate a prognostic effect shared by both arms from one specific to cases, and time-dependent AUC via timeROC at horizons chosen from the observed follow-up distribution; (T1S3) the report with the reproducibility record. Two honesty constraints are built into the steps. First, the 20-gene signature was not derived here, so no feature selection happens on these samples and the Cox estimate is not optimistic on that account — but if the signature was originally derived on this same cohort (unknown from the profile), the step must say so rather than present the hazard ratio as validated. Second, power comes from the events, not from the 120 samples: the number of events is unknown until T3S5 reads the metadata, and if events are few (roughly under 10 per covariate) the step reports the model as underpowered and descriptive rather than confirmatory. The salmon import state is unknown; the plan does no length correction it cannot justify and works from the counts as delivered, which is acceptable here because the analysis is within-gene across samples (filtering, TMM, per-sample ranks) and never compares genes to each other on an absolute scale — T1S2 states this assumption.

steps.method: blind VST, PCA on top variable genes, sample distance heatmap
TMM scaling factors then logCPM for scoring
UCell rank-based signature scores per sample
Cox proportional hazards model on the signature score with condition as covariate

Routed to the statistical-modeling agent because the primary data object is a per-sample score table plus time/event, not a count matrix.

steps.name: Report and reproducibility record
steps.question: What does this cohort say about the association between the 20-gene signature score and time to event, adjusted for case versus control status, and under what caveats?
steps.description: Assemble a single report from T1S1, T1S2, T3S1 and T3S5: the QC figures, the number of genes retained by filterByExpr out of 12000, the number of the 20 signature genes actually scored, the score distribution by condition, and the Cox results — hazard ratio per SD with CI, the condition term, the PH diagnostics, the interaction test, the C-index and the timeROC AUCs. Lead with the answer to the research question in one sentence, then the evidence. State the limitations: the unknown Salmon length-correction state, the absence of clinical covariates beyond condition in the 4-column metadata, the events-per-variable ratio, and the absence of an external validation cohort. Include the reproducibility record: sessionInfo, package versions, the random seed of any step using randomness, and the signature source and gene count.
steps.context: Final synthesis step. It performs no new inference and must not upgrade any descriptive finding into a confirmatory claim.
acceptance_criteria: The report opens with a direct answer to whether the signature score associates with time to event after adjusting for condition, including the effect size and its uncertainty
All numbers in the report trace to an upstream step; no new analysis is introduced
Limitations are stated explicitly: unknown length-correction state, only condition available as a covariate, events-per-variable ratio, no external validation
A reproducibility record with sessionInfo, package versions and seeds is included
constraints: Do not run new statistical tests in this step
Do not present the Kaplan-Meier tertile curves as inferential evidence
If the Cox result was flagged underpowered in T3S5, carry that label into the headline sentence
caveats: A single-cohort association without external validation is not a qualified biomarker and must not be described as one

grounding.reason: No rule covers the report step itself; the reproducibility record follows R-0086@becf

steps.method: blind VST, PCA on top variable genes, sample distance heatmap
TMM scaling factors then logCPM for scoring
UCell rank-based signature scores per sample
Cox proportional hazards model on the signature score with condition as covariate
